account: So far, today looks mostly routine, and I have not found clear evidence of anything secret. I attended my morning office hours and market walk, went home for noon, and returned to town hall for the thirteen-hundred accounts appointment. Most market visitors said they had no news. Townsfolk 28 and 18 reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery; that sounds like ordinary baking supplies, not evidence of an unusual plan. The builder is now inside town hall near me, carrying a lantern even though it is daytime. I do not know why the builder is visiting or what the lantern is for. The main unresolved oddity is my fifteen-hundred tea appointment: the appointment book gives only 'the neighbour' at an east-bank dockside cottage, with neither a name nor an exact cottage. The secretary did not know the host either and said she would confirm the details. The same vague tea appointment appears tomorrow. It could simply be an incompletely recorded social engagement; I cannot yet connect it to the baker or builder. The secretary took the appointment book this morning, and a written book is now back in the appointments chest, but I have not read it again to see whether she added clarification. I still feel out of the loop, but I do not yet know of any coordinated undertaking or its purpose.
